item.title: A Frequency-Learning Interpolation-Based Coordinate Descent Method to Optimize Parameterized Quantum Circuits on Quantum Hardware
item.description:
Skim new method — Online frequency learning for coordinate descent in VQAs scales to 100 qubits on IBM quantum hardware. Adapts interpolation frequencies and shot counts via a relative error parameter εrel, matching or outperforming fixed-frequency ICD and COBYLA.

Grade 0.466 · 2.7σ above the day's baseline · matched “The Variational Quantum Eigensolver: A review of methods and best practices”

Figure

Convergence comparison showing average objective function value versus total quantum shots for FLICD, COBYLA, and ICD across layers p∈{1,2,5} on a 20-vertex graph.

Asks

Can coordinate-descent structure-aware optimizers learn interpolation frequencies online and optimize parameterized quantum circuits on noisy hardware at scale?

Before

Interpolation-based Coordinate Descent (ICD) required manually preselected fixed frequency sets and constant shot counts, with hardware demonstrations restricted to ≤6 qubits (or up to 32 trapped-ion qubits for Jacobi iteration).

But

Evaluated exclusively on linear-chain QAOA instances for MaxCut problems up to 100 qubits and depth p≤5.

Tools

Frequency-Learning Interpolation-Based Coordinate Descent (FLICD) · IBM Heron processor (`ibm_rensselaer`) · LC-QAOA ansatz · Least-squares oversampled trigonometric interpolation

Abstract

Structure-aware optimizers have been the focus of recent study for the optimization of parameters in variational quantum circuits. Many of these optimizers follow a coordinate-based paradigm, making single parameter updates by using classical approximations to the cost function generated from quantum sampling. However, the performance of structure-aware optimizers on real quantum hardware at large system size has yet to be demonstrated. Recently, Interpolation-based Coordinate Descent (ICD) has been proposed to unify many of these optimizers into one framework. ICD requires a preset frequency set for interpolation, which can be theoretically derived, but for which the cost function is generally sparse over and may require manual tuning. To address these issues, we propose Frequency-learning Interpolation-based Coordinate Descent (FLICD) to adaptively learn frequencies online, allowing easier scaling up to larger systems. We demonstrate that our algorithm is more accurate than an existing zeroth-order method COBYLA and requires fewer quantum resources than ICD on simulator. Using IBM quantum hardware, we execute FLICD on systems up to 100 qubits and observe robust performance with an increasing number of layers.

arxave:action.title: Test FLICD on the spin-qubit QPU for a QAOA benchmark

item.arxave:action: Run a small QAOA/MaxCut instance on the spin-qubit machine and compare FLICD against COBYLA and ICD in total shots and wall-clock time, including the HPC-QPU communication overhead.
